headline: Acquisitions lift revenue as a rough year-ago comp fades
summary_short: Revenue rose 9.0% y/y and 2.5% q/q to $430.5M on recent acquisitions and lease escalations, while diluted EPS of $0.80 was flat-to-down q/q but up 48.1% y/y as last year's outsized CECL credit-loss provision didn't repeat.
summary_long: Total income from real estate rose to $430.5 million (+9.0% y/y, +2.5% q/q) on $38.7 million of incremental rent from recent acquisitions (Bally's Lincoln, PENN's Hollywood Casino Aurora relocation) and lease escalations, partly offset by unfavorable straight-line rent adjustments. Net income of $228.4 million was +50.8% y/y but -1.5% q/q — the y/y jump reflects a much smaller CECL credit-loss provision ($3.0 million vs $53.7 million a year ago), while the q/q dip reflects a bigger provision benefit in Q1 2026. Interest expense rose 12.0% y/y on acquisition-related borrowings. Cash grew to $319.0 million; long-term debt rose to $8.08 billion after an $800 million senior-notes issuance. No formal guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Recent acquisitions (Bally's Lincoln, PENN's Hollywood Casino Aurora relocation) increased cash rental income by $38.7 million, plus lease escalations added $4.5 million, partly offset by unfavorable straight-line rent adjustments of $7.9 million.

GLPI doesn't report a GAAP 'gross profit' line; this Yahoo-derived subtotal moves with the same revenue growth and operating-expense decline (lower CECL provision) described under Revenue and Operating income.

Total operating expenses fell $54.7 million as the year-ago quarter's $53.7 million CECL credit-loss provision (from a more pessimistic economic forecast) shrank to $3.0 million this quarter, plus lower G&A on lower stock-based compensation costs.

Interest expense rose $10.8 million y/y on increased borrowings that partially funded our recent acquisitions, partially offsetting the operating-income gain from the collapsed CECL provision; the q/q dip reflects a smaller Q2 credit-loss benefit than Q1 2026's.

The y/y increase was primarily attributable to lower operating expenses (the provision-driven $54.7 million decline) and higher revenue, partly offset by higher interest expense; the q/q dip reflects a smaller current-quarter credit-loss benefit than Q1 2026 booked.
Follows net income's y/y increase (described above) divided by a weighted-average basic share count that grew only modestly, from recent equity issuance under the 2025 ATM program.
Same net-income-driven increase as basic EPS; dilution from the 2025 ATM forward-sale settlement (7.6 million shares issued June 1, 2026) was more than offset by the underlying earnings growth.

Cash fell y/y mainly because June 2025's balance was inflated by the maturity of zero coupon U.S. Treasury Bills totaling $550.0 million, which didn't recur; cash grew q/q on the $800 million senior-notes issuance and a $351 million forward-sale settlement.
Debt rose on an $800 million issuance of 5.625% Senior Notes due 2036, used to repay the 2022 Term Loan and fund working capital and general corporate purposes.
Equity growth reflects retained net income plus $351 million of net proceeds from settling a 2025 ATM Program forward-sale agreement, partly offset by common dividends paid.

Recent acquisitions and lease escalations lifted revenue, while a swing in the CECL credit-loss provision drove net income sharply higher y/y; management expects future growth to come from funding commitments and new acquisitions, and gave no formal guidance.
